idiom_name: typed asynchronous queue instead of a blocking wait (no runtime suspension)
implementation_notes: TypeScript adds types, not a runtime: the guarantees are JavaScript's, and a main-thread wait is impossible (Atomics.wait throws when the calling thread cannot be blocked; blocking exists only inside worker threads), so the monitor form cannot be typed into existence. What the type system does contribute is a guard that is hard to misuse: an AsyncQueue<T> whose take(): Promise<T> must be awaited, an AsyncGenerator<T> consumed with for await, and AbortSignal/deadline parameters make the wait and its cancellation explicit, whereas the classic monitor invariant has no type-level representation. Express the suspension as awaiting a handoff (Async Method Invocation) and re-check the condition after every await, because another task can consume the value while the awaiting task is queued.
pitfalls: Types cannot enforce the guard: a consumer that forgets to re-check the condition after await still compiles and still races.
Atomics.wait needs a SharedArrayBuffer and a worker thread, and browsers expose SharedArrayBuffer only under cross-origin isolation.
Awaiting inside a loop that also mutates the guarded state can interleave with other tasks between check and use, so publish state transitions through the queue itself.
alternative: Model the guard as an awaited handoff with types: an AsyncQueue<T>/AsyncGenerator<T> whose take() returns Promise<T> (Async Method Invocation), plus AbortSignal/deadline arguments for bounded waits; use Atomics.wait/waitAsync over a SharedArrayBuffer only inside worker threads.
